locator: The passage on 1736 S. Prairie Avenue: its completion in 1864 for Granville S. Ingraham, its mansard, Ingraham's career and sale of the house, and Hugh McBirney's long residence.

note: Read: 'One house of note was completed in 1864, the large brick house at 1736 S. Prairie Avenue, for Granville S. Ingraham.' The next sentence opens 'Surviving photos show a third-story mansard roof which may well have been a later addition' and goes on to call the house beneath it a standard Italianate house of the Civil War years (paraphrased here, not quoted). Ingraham 'came to Chicago in 1856 and made a fortune as a wholesale grocer'; he 'sold the house long before his death at his winter home in Pass Christian, Mississippi in 1892'; the house 'is best remembered today as the long-time residence of lead manufacturer Hugh McBirney.' The post gives no date for the mansard, and its 'may well have been' is the author's judgement from the photographs, not a record of building.
what_it_supplies: that 1736 was a large brick house completed in 1864 for Granville S. Ingraham
the author's judgement that its mansard may well have been a later addition to an Italianate house
that Hugh McBirney lived in it for many years
what_it_does_not_supply: anything of the flank, the rear or the alley building
